justification: The DCP commit worker decides whether a human-approved chapter goes live. Its candidate query took the approval's PDF fingerprint and its count of fingerprints over every queue row, including superseded and rejected history, so any chapter that had been reviewed before on an older PDF was skipped as a mixed or stale approval. A wrong answer here silently keeps reviewed rules off the product, or, if loosened too far, lets a genuinely mixed approval through.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: A chapter with approved rows on the current PDF plus superseded or rejected rows on an older PDF is reported with more than one fingerprint, or dated to the older PDF; or approvals that really span two PDFs stop being reported as two; or a pending row, or a rejection on the current PDF, stops blocking.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Against the unfixed query the new file printed '2 failed, 2 passed' (superseded and rejected history each gave hash_variants 2). With the fix all 4 pass, and the 22 existing commit-worker tests still pass (26 in total).
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Production measurement 2026-09-15: every Woollahra chapter had 2-3 distinct source_content_hash values across its dcp_review_queue rows but exactly 1 among its approved rows (query over dcp_review_queue joined to dcp_chapter_registry, grouped by council and chapter).

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_review_queue.status is constrained to pending, in_progress, approved, rejected, needs_info, superseded; enqueue_review_changes marks rejected rows superseded on re-read and never deletes approved rows, so history on older fingerprints accumulates by design.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The skip message says 'approved rows span multiple source hashes', but the aggregates were not filtered to approved rows, while the neighbouring approved and blocking counts were.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Two FILTER clauses on the existing query; no new query, table or column.

functions.name: find_committable_chapters
functions.input: A cursor on the production database.
functions.output: One dict per active chapter that has approved rows and nothing blocking, with approved_hash (the fingerprint of its approved rows) and hash_variants (how many fingerprints its approved rows carry).
functions.if_none: A chapter with no approved rows is not returned; an approved row with a NULL fingerprint leaves approved_hash NULL, which the caller already treats as a legacy approval.

values.if_missing: hash_variants 0 or NULL skips the multi-fingerprint guard only when there are no fingerprints to compare; approved_hash NULL skips the currency comparison as before.

queries.purpose: List chapters whose review is complete: approved rows exist, nothing pending or rejected on the current PDF, and the fingerprints of the approved rows only.
queries.where_clause: FROM dcp_review_queue q JOIN dcp_chapter_registry r ON r.council = q.council AND r.chapter_key = q.chapter_key AND r.is_active = TRUE GROUP BY q.council, q.chapter_key HAVING approved > 0 AND blocking = 0 -- MAX and COUNT(DISTINCT) of source_content_hash now FILTER (WHERE q.status = 'approved')

break_it.scenario: Chapters reviewed once, re-read after their PDF changed, and whose new rows were approved; the old rows sit as superseded on the old fingerprint, so the list of chapters whose review is complete leaves them out.
break_it.what_happens: Before, the worker counted two fingerprints and skipped the chapter forever; the reviewed rules never went live.
break_it.how: Both aggregates count approved rows only; test_superseded_history_on_an_older_pdf_does_not_block_the_current_approval.

break_it.scenario: The old fingerprint sorts after the current one, so an unfiltered MAX names the old PDF as the approval's source.
break_it.what_happens: The currency guard then calls a current approval stale and skips it.
break_it.how: The test's older hash is chosen to sort last; reverting the MAX filter alone fails 2 tests.

break_it.scenario: Approved rows really do come from two versions of the PDF.
break_it.what_happens: Committing would mix rules read from different versions of the plan.
break_it.how: Confusable negative: test_approvals_that_span_two_pdfs_are_still_reported_as_two keeps hash_variants at 2, so the existing skip still fires.

break_it.scenario: A row is still pending, or a rejection sits on the current PDF.
break_it.how: Blocking logic unchanged; test_a_pending_row_or_a_rejection_on_the_current_pdf_still_blocks runs the real query.

mutation_analysis: The new tests run the worker's real SQL against in-memory SQLite (which supports COUNT(DISTINCT) FILTER and MAX FILTER); the existing tests stub find_committable_chapters and never ran it. Two mutations on the working copy, restored after: hash_variants FILTER removed -> 2 failed; approved_hash FILTER removed -> 2 failed. Unmutated: 4 of 4 new tests and 26 of 26 commit-worker tests pass.
residual_risk: SQLite and Postgres agree on these aggregates but not on every SQL feature; a future edit using Postgres-only syntax in this query would make the test error rather than pass. Approvals left as 'approved' on an older PDF still count among approved rows, so a chapter holding both old and new approvals is still skipped until the old ones are marked superseded - that is the mixed-approval guard doing its job, not this bug.

post_merge.manual_verify: After deploy, python scripts/dcp_commit_approved.py (dry run) should list chapters with old review history as [would commit] rather than '[skip] ... multiple source hashes'.
